svg.aria-label: An illustrative hunt. From a ransomware report, a supervisor agent splits the hunt among narrow agents, each given only the tools and context its one job needs, because a local model does best with one job: forming a hypothesis, writing and running the detection logic, reporting. Agents carry tools and skills. The Detection agent's first search, for schtasks.exe, comes back empty, and empty does not mean safe: tasks made through the Task Scheduler API never launch schtasks.exe, so the agent asks whether its search could have missed the threat, checks a new query and searches another way, around event 4698, a task being created. That returns every task created; analysing them surfaces one unusual task, \WinTaskUpdate, on one host and not in the baseline. The Reporting agent writes it up with the evidence attached, and only a human analyst makes the call.

g.text: Agentic Threat Hunting|From a ransomware report to one lead
Hunch: attackers hide in scheduled tasks
A local model does best with one job, so
each narrow agent gets only the tools
looks for the tool by name
no match: attackers can skip that tool
now looks for the action: a new task
one new task doesn't match the rest
No results can mean a bad query, not a
safe network. So the agent rewrites it,
checks the fix and searches again.
Agents flag what looks suspicious, with
the evidence attached. Only a human
